title: Ice creep constitutive (Glen flow law) + Norton power-law validation surface + long-time contact force relaxation
decision: Accept src/tensordem/creep_constitutive.py as the tensor-level creep kernel for TensorDEM ice contacts if and only if every pre-registered threshold below is met by tools/run_creep_validation.py and the pytest surface.

alternatives.A_rejected: Reuse ice_bond_viscoelastic Maxwell-Wiechert (Prony) law: linear, so it cannot represent the sigma^n rate sensitivity of ice (n ~ 3) and cannot produce a ductile exponent.
alternatives.B_rejected: Explicit (forward Euler) Norton update: unconditionally unstable for the large A sigma^n dt of the contact problem and gives no path to an energy ledger; kept only as the conceptual baseline.
alternatives.C_chosen: Implicit backward-Euler J2 radial return on the Glen flow law with a scalar bracketed Newton solve; closed-form anchors for every stage (Norton creep, Bailey/Norton relaxation, Kachanov tertiary, Hertz constant-displacement relaxation).

hypothesis.H1: The work-conjugate Glen form eps_dot_ij = (3/2) A sigma_eq^(n-1) s_ij reduces exactly to eps_dot = A sigma^n under uniaxial stress for all n in [2.5, 3.5].
hypothesis.H2: Backward-Euler radial return reproduces the closed-form Norton relaxation to first order in dt, and the fixed-total-strain vs free-lateral relaxation moduli (3G vs E) are distinguishable (a 15% gap, not a bug).
hypothesis.H3: A two-sphere Hertz contact at fixed centre distance relaxes F(t)/F0 to the separable closed form F/F0 = (delta_e/delta0)^(3/2) within 5% at t = 100 s.
hypothesis.H4: The three-stage curve requires Bailey primary hardening + Kachanov damage: a pure Norton law has no primary and no tertiary stage (falsifiable negative control).

a_integrator_relaxation.metric: max |sigma_num/sigma_closed_form - 1| on the same 10 cases (dt = t_end/500)

b_primary_exponent.metric: |fitted log-log slope - 1/3|/(1/3), window t in [1, 100] s

b_steady_rate.metric: |mean rate / (A sigma^n) - 1| in the steady window t > 3e4 s

b_tertiary.metric: strictly increasing rate after 0.9 t_r AND rate(t->t_r)/A sigma^n > 10, plus rupture time rel. error

c_contact_relaxation.metric: |F(t)/F0 numeric - closed form| / closed form at t = 100 s, dt = 0.04 s (convergence shown for dt in {5, 1, 0.2, 0.04})
c_contact_relaxation.baseline: separable Hertz creep relaxation closed form

d_energy_ledger.metric: |dU + int sigma:eps_dot_c dt| / |dU| (fixed displacement, zero external work)

f_tests.metric: pytest test count in tests/test_creep_constitutive.py with analytic anchors and negative controls

exclusions: No time-dependent temperature: A is constant per case (Glen A(T) is out of scope, declared as a limitation).
Creep is incompressible; volumetric creep and damage-induced dilatancy are not modelled.
The contact creep-active depth h = c_h * a is a modelling assumption (c_h = 1 default), stated in the report; the closed form is parametric in c_h, so the comparison does not depend on its value.
Homogeneous stress in the contact patch: grain-scale stress heterogeneity and Hertz pressure redistribution are not modelled.
stopping_rule: Run the sweep once; if a threshold fails, report honest FAIL with the measured number and do not tune parameters to pass. Timestep refinements are pre-declared (dt in {5, 1, 0.2, 0.04} s and {1, 0.5} s for the element) and are the only permitted repetitions.
environment_control: float64 throughout; units MPa / s / mm (force N, energy mJ); torch 2.7.1, numpy 2.4.6, matplotlib 3.10.8; single-threaded serial determinism (no randomness anywhere in the node).
analysis: Aggregation = max relative error per criterion; no outlier removal; all 10 sweep cases reported individually in artifacts/in69_n01_creep/summary.json.
